newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan report better than expected.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan report better than expected.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. Thursday reported lower earnings in the first quarter, but strong results from the investment bank's trading operations, however, helped its profits beat Wall Street expectations.

New York-based J. P. Morgan said its net income was $424 million for the first quarter, down from $439 million a year ago. Earnings per share fell to $2.04 per share from $2.13 a share a year ago, but still topped analysts' expectations of $1.92 per share, as compiled by First Call.
Overall, J.P. Morgan's first quarter revenue rose 5 percent to $1.83 billion from $1.74 billion.
The company said total return in proprietary investing and trading was $365 million vs. $106 million a year ago.
The higher trading revenue was partially offset by lower net interest revenue from investing activities due to the maturing of higher-yielding investments.
J.P. Morgan said revenue in its finance and advisory business, including debt and equity underwriting, rose 8 percent in the first quarter to $451 million.

J.P. Morgan said in its market-making business, revenues totalled $733 million, down from $771 million. The company said most markets showed strength early in the quarter, but activity slowed in mid-March as a result of the quarter percentage point increase in short-term interest rates by the Federal Reserve.
In its asset management and servicing business, J.P. Morgan said revenues rose 9 percent to $375 million in the first quarter.
In emerging markets, revenues rose nearly 50 percent to $186 million, while commodities revenues fell to $12 million from $31 million a year ago.
J. P. Morgan stock was up $1.25 to $99.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
